In layout.json, tag the masthead title and the 'IOWA CITY, IOWA' line as their own kinds (title/location) rather than header/subheader: right now the header level shows two sizes (h 17.46 vs 10.32 mm) and three x positions (12.7/29.89/112.18), and the subheader level shows two styles (h 4.23 vs 3.97 mm, x 86.85), so the per-level check fails on paper even though the render is correct.

Make each section-header element box match its 24 pt slot (it is 10.32 mm = 29.25 pt now), so that box-based measurement of the space below Cider (1.85 mm to the item) agrees with the 12 pt slot gap you declared and with the other sections (10.31 mm to the subheader).

Anchor the right-column end mark (rules and three diamonds) to the column grid, either left-aligned at 318 pt or spanning the full 258 pt measure, instead of floating centred in a short rule, so it reads as part of the column structure.

top_problem: The two columns' headers do not line up. At a 12 pt baseline grid that is two grid steps, not a real alignment, so it reads as accidental. Everything else in my lens measures clean. Headers have one size (24 pt) and one x per column (36 and 318 pt). Subheaders have one style and sit at the same x as the headers. The gap below every header is 12 pt, including Cider. The space above every header is 36 pt. The kicker baselines match the header baselines (delta 0.00 pt). Items to the next subheader measure 24 pt everywhere, which I confirmed on the preview.

Wine will then share a line with Spirits, By the Glass with Agave and Sparkling with Brandy, and Brut Rosé's description will end on the same baseline as Cognac VSOP's, so the columns are cross-aligned and still bottom-balanced at 720 pt.

Either give it a matching subheader row (for example 'DRAFT' or 'ON TAP', if that is verified) so every section has the same header, subheader and item rhythm, or fold it into Beer as a 'CIDER' subheader and re-balance the columns.

Raise the subheaders from 8.5 pt to 9 pt, or loosen the tracking slightly. At 8.5 pt with 2 pt tracking, teal on cream is the weakest level in the hierarchy next to the 13 pt item names and 24 pt headers, and on the phone it risks reading as a caption rather than a section label.

lens: palette, contrast, price and number styling
top_problem: The palette and contrast pass every check (text 14.69:1, prices #A63C1A 5.55:1, subheaders 6.5:1, descriptions 7.33:1; marigold is used only on non-text ornaments). The measured checks all pass: margins are 36.0 pt on all sides (maximum ink deviation 0.08 mm); item x is 12.70 / 112.18 mm; price right edges are 103.71-103.72 / 203.20 mm (spread 0.01 mm); all 66 baselines sit at 12k + 9 pt; every gap is 12 pt or 24 pt; headers share one x per column.

Label the Sparkling price 'glass' or 'bottle' (or carry it in the subheader, e.g. 'SPARKLING · GLASS') once confirmed, and put the pour or volume in the 'BY THE GLASS' subheader so every wine number has a unit.

Merge the two near-identical reds (flags #B4441F and text #A63C1A) into one terracotta, darkening the flags to #A63C1A, so the palette reads as three deliberate hues plus neutrals rather than two slightly different reds.

Rebalance the right column: fold the one-item Cider section into Beer as a 'CIDER' subheader (or give it a second item), and centre the diamond endmark on the full measure or mirror it in the left column, so the right column doesn't end with an off-axis ornament and a heavy header over a single line.
Put the real venue name in the display title in place of the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' so the masthead, palette and papel picado read as one branded piece.

lens: ornament and elevating elements vs top-agency menu work
top_problem: The ornaments are well executed, but they are generic 'fiesta' stock rather than a signature system. The papel picado is nine solid rectangles, each with a centred clip-art icon (star, heart, moon, cactus) and a dotted hem, not real cut-paper lace. The end marks are applied to one column only (three diamonds on the right, nothing on the left). A top agency would not sign that as a bespoke identity. The measured checks all pass: margins 36/36/36/36 pt (ink R 35.76, 0.08 mm off), one item x and one price right edge per column (spread 0.0 mm), every gap a multiple of 12 pt, 66 baselines on the 12 pt grid, contrast 5.55 to 14.69:1 for text.
fixes: Redraw the papel picado as true pierced lace: negative-space cut-work with a scalloped or fringed hem and a slight drape on the string. Drop the icon-font style motifs (star, heart, moon, and especially the Tex-Mex cactus) in favour of one or two related motifs taken from the agave used in the footer.
Make the end marks symmetric and purposeful: give the left column the same three-diamond end mark as the right, or remove it from both and let the footer agave rule close the page.

Replace the generic double rule under the title with a bespoke device from the same system (for example a thin rule broken by a small agave or diamond cluster), so that the flags, rule, kickers and footer read as one ornament family.

Add one tactile layer that lifts the flat cream: a subtle paper or plaster grain, or a faint oversized agave or talavera watermark behind the empty lower right of Beer/Cider. Keep text contrast at 4.5:1 or higher.

Fill the dead zones under Amber Lager and Dry Cider, where the right column has visibly larger voids than the left despite equal measured gaps. Use a small ornamented call-out (for example a boxed 'Michelada or shot-and-beer' style panel if the data supports it) or rebalance the sections so that whitespace reads as intentional.

top_problem: The phone view stacks the print columns in order, so Spirits comes before Beer, Cider and Wine. The one-item Cider section becomes a thin interruption, and nothing in the one-column flow is rethought for the phone. The measured grid, margins, left edges and price columns all pass: margins 36/36/36/36 pt (ink max deviation 0.08 mm), one name x per column (36 and 318 pt), one price right edge per column (294 and 576 pt, 0.0 mm spread), a constant 12 pt item gap and 12 pt below every header. Contrast is at least 4.5:1: roughly 9:1 for muted #5A4A3F, 5.5:1 for accent #A63C1A and 6.5:1 for secondary #2F5D50 on #F6EEDF.
fixes: Reorder the phone single column to Cocktails, Beer, Cider, Wine, Spirits (or move Spirits into the right column in print too) so both formats follow the cocktails-beer-wine-spirits flow the scorecard expects.

Merge Cider into Beer as a 'Cider' subheader, under the same drawn-rule style as 'Draft', so neither format has a one-item top-level section with a large empty band around it (print right column, about 110 px at 300 dpi above Cider and Wine).

Carry the print's three-diamond endmark (gold, terracotta, green) into the phone view before the ¡Salud! footer, and on the phone cut the papel picado banner to 5-6 larger flags so each motif reads at 390 px rather than 9 tiny ones.

Fix the phone description wraps that leave a short tail ('D.O. Tequila.' under Añejo, 'Stirred and strained into a coupe.' pattern) by tightening the phone description measure or adding non-breaking spaces so no line ends with a dangling two-word fragment.

On the phone, raise the Spanish kickers from 8 pt to about 9 pt and baseline-lock them to the header so 'CÓCTELES / DESTILADOS' read as a deliberate secondary label rather than floating mid-height beside the 24 pt header.

lens: every item and price vs the draft (build/draft_doc.json rev 3)
